mainEntity.name: Will composite bonding on one front tooth look natural?

acceptedAnswer.text: In many cases, yes. A skilled and experienced dentist can carefully match the shade, translucency, and shape of composite resin to blend seamlessly with your surrounding teeth. The result depends on the quality of shade assessment and the clinician's technique. During your consultation, your dentist should be able to discuss what outcome is realistic for your specific situation and show you examples of previous work where appropriate.

mainEntity.name: Is composite bonding on a front tooth painful?

acceptedAnswer.text: Composite bonding is generally a comfortable procedure. Because it typically requires minimal or no preparation of natural tooth enamel, local anaesthesia is not always necessary, though it can be used if preferred. Most patients report little to no discomfort during or after the procedure. If you experience any sensitivity following bonding, this is usually mild and temporary, but you should contact your dentist if it persists.

mainEntity.name: How much does composite bonding on one tooth cost in London?

acceptedAnswer.text: The cost of composite bonding on a single tooth varies between dental practices and depends on the complexity of the case, the experience of the clinician, and the materials used. As this is a cosmetic treatment, it is not available on the NHS and is provided privately. The best approach is to attend a consultation where your dentist can assess your needs and provide a clear, transparent treatment plan with associated costs.

mainEntity.name: Can composite bonding fix a chipped front tooth?

acceptedAnswer.text: Composite bonding is commonly used to repair chipped front teeth and is often an appropriate option for this purpose. The resin is applied to rebuild the missing portion of the tooth, shaped to match the natural contour, and polished to a smooth finish. The suitability of bonding for a chipped tooth depends on the extent of the chip and the structural integrity of the remaining tooth, which your dentist will assess during examination.

mainEntity.name: Does composite bonding stain over time?

acceptedAnswer.text: Composite resin can absorb pigments from food and drink more readily than natural tooth enamel over time. Regular consumption of coffee, tea, red wine, and certain foods may cause gradual discolouration. Maintaining good oral hygiene, attending professional hygiene appointments, and avoiding prolonged contact with staining substances can help minimise this. Your dentist can advise on polishing or maintenance at routine check-up appointments.

mainEntity.name: Can I have teeth whitening after composite bonding?

acceptedAnswer.text: Composite resin does not respond to whitening agents, so if you are considering teeth whitening and composite bonding, it is generally recommended to whiten your teeth first. Your dentist can then shade-match the bonding material to your post-whitening tooth colour. Attempting to whiten teeth after bonding has been placed will result in your natural teeth becoming lighter while the composite resin remains its original shade, creating a mismatch.
